notes: Volume A–C of the collection: 118 pages, 73 biographies of architects, builders, engineers, landscape architects, preservationists and firms whose names begin A, B or C, read end to end — the title and letter-index pages, every biography (education, firms, cultural identification, narrative, footnotes), every 'Projects in San Francisco' and 'Other notable projects' list, and every figure caption. The collection is eight PDFs on one landing page (A–C, D–F, G–I, J–L, M–O, P–R, S–U, V–Z) plus a case report; this batch is the first volume only. There is no inventory table and no APN anywhere in the document. The 'Projects in San Francisco' lists are the dense seam: 66 of the 73 entries carry one, and nearly every line is an address, a year and a building name already attached to a named practitioner. That is what makes a document with no inventory the densest this source has produced — 505 numbered-address mentions across 118 pages, roughly one every four lines of list.

coverage.note: 505 numbered-address mentions across 118 pages became 412 findings. The gap is deduplication, not sampling: the same project list is reprinted under each partner and again under the firm (Anshen + Allen's thirteen San Francisco projects appear three times, Appleton & Wolfard's libraries twice, Campbell & Wong's houses twice, Amandes and Clausen's partnership work twice), and figure captions repeat an address the list already gave. Each project was recorded once, credited to the firm where the volume has a firm entry. 353 of the 412 reached a parcel and 59 did not: 25 numbers the city no longer has (mostly pre-1906 downtown buildings), 18 recorded ranges now split across separate parcels, 14 condominium parcels, 1 street the address register does not hold (Jose Sarria Court) and 1 located only as One Maritime Plaza. Of the 353, 317 were published onto 312 pages and 36 declined: 23 where the page already carried the same attribution from a neighbouring survey, 7 whose parcel has no 2025 secured-roll row so the seeder will not make a page, and 6 undated office-occupancy or engineering credits with no component on the page to carry them. Addresses NOT recorded, and why: intersections with no street number ('California at Kearny Streets', 'Mason at O'Farrell', 'Powell Street and O'Farrell Street', 'Clay and Divisadero Streets', 'Harrison Street and 2nd Street', '15th Street and Julian Avenue', '16th Street and Prosper Street', 'Market Street and Battery Street', 'Bush and Gough Street', 'Pine and Pierce Streets', 'Jackson and Battery Streets', 'Leavenworth and Greenwich Streets', 'Jones and Geary Streets', 'Franklin & Geary', 'Pacific and Powell Streets', 'Van Ness Avenue and Sutter Street'); projects the volume itself marks 'unknown address' (the Doty, Zanetti, Hutchinson, Rothermel, Walker, Sanburn, Campbell, Josselyn, Beale and Hopkins commissions, Union Bank of San Francisco, Lucky Market, the Stiavelli flat, Holly Park Housing, the Golden Gateway Phase I townhouses); places named without a number (the Ferry Building, World Trade Club at '1 Ferry Building', Washington Square, Portsmouth Square, Golden Gate Park and the Hall of Flowers at '9th Avenue in Golden Gate Park', Strybing Arboretum, Parkmerced, Potrero Terrace, Graystone Terrace Apartments, the Southern Crossing, Treasure Island and the 1939 Exposition, the Embarcadero Center master plan, the Fisherman's Wharf and South Bayshore plans, the Civic Center plan, the BART stations, the '31st Avenue tract', the '2100 block tract on 33rd Avenue', the '28th Avenue houses', 'twelve homes in Sea Cliff', and the fifteen hillside residences at Leavenworth and Greenwich); and every address outside San Francisco (Berkeley, Oakland, Stanford, Palo Alto, Sausalito, San Anselmo, Ross, Daly City, Millbrae, Richmond, Santa Cruz, Bishop, Redding, Bear Lake, Los Angeles, Hollywood, Charleston, Ogden, Harrisburg, Beijing, Shenzhen, Paris). Addresses seen and deliberately not recorded under the people rule, because the only fact attached is where a person lived: 27 Fountain Street and the 100 block of Granville Way (Christian Anderson), 855 Chestnut Street (John Bakewell Jr.), 2990 Vallejo Street (Walter Bliss), 2229 Webster Street (Anne Bloomfield), 822 Noe Street (John Baumann), 290 Sea Cliff Avenue as a residence (recorded instead as an Earle Bertz design), and 1422 27th Avenue and 1399 21st Avenue as homes (1422 recorded instead as a Christensen build). Three recorded building names were dropped at publication for the same reason, the address and the credit kept: the Charles Crocker house at 1100 California Street, the Clunie House at 301 Lyon Street and the Clunie Estate at 519 California Street.
